Categories.value: Taken with Pentax Optio S50|Korea Railroad Museum|Railway coaches of South Korea|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR|Files uploaded by Kobac|Train interiors in South Korea|Files from InSapphoWeTrust Flickr stream|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|South Korea photographs taken on 2008-11-28|Orbit fans|Train electric fans

ImageDescription.value:
This is the interior of the Tongil (Unification) Class passenger car, seating 72.

Car 13101 was built in 1965, the first of a new design of passenger cars with weight reduced from 36 metric tons to 30 to save on fuel and energy costs. Also unlike earlier passenger cars, seats can be rotated in the direction of travel for improved comfort. In colder months, a boiler car attached to the train provided heat, but in the summer, the only means of cooling were open windows and overhead fans.

The Tongil represented express-class service, slotting below air-conditioned higher-level express trains but above the basic commuter train, the Bidulgwi (Dove) class.

EAST CHINA SEA (March 27, 2014) Machinist’s Mate Fireman Chase Owen, from Oxford, N.C., lights a boiler aboard the amphibious assault ship USS Bonhomme Richard (LHD 6). Bonhomme Richard is the flagship of the Bonhomme Richard Amphibious Ready Group and is participating in Exercise Ssang Yong, an annual combined exercise with the Republic of Korea.
